title: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build a reusable staged-release safety harness that combines lightweight canaries, percent-based traffic ramps, feature-flag gates, synthetic traffic checks, and automated rollback actions. This harness should be pluggable into Redwood's runtime and Console, support both Hosted and Dedicated deployments, and be compatible with Private (VPC) rollouts. The design must allow per-route and per-model policies, expose a clear audit trail, and provide measurable SLO-based pass/fail signals for automated decisions.

Deliverables: a feature-flag controller API, a traffic-ramp controller integrated with the routing layer, a small state machine service for gate evaluations, predefined gate templates (latency/error/quality/regression), Console UI hooks for visualization, runbook + playbook for manual override, and a demo rollout on an internal non-prod model serving path.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Canary flow can be started from Console or API and will route 1% of traffic to the new version within 5 minutes.
2) System evaluates gates (p95 latency, 5xx rate, decode-error rate, and quality regression against golden prompts) and emits pass/fail decisions to Console timeline.
3) When any gate fails above configured threshold, the controller executes a rollback action within 30s and records the reason in audit logs.
4) Operators can override automation via Console, pausing or accelerating ramps.
5) Integration tests simulate synthetic traffic and verify auto-rollback triggers for injected faults.
6) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (design & proto, 2 sprints): API and controller prototype; gate templates; unit tests.
Phase B (integration, 2 sprints): integrate with routing layer, Console UI, and metrics pipeline; end-to-end smoke tests.
Phase C (canary on internal model, 1 sprint): run 2 internal rollouts, validate thresholds, observe false-positive rate.
Phase D (limited external customers + docs): opt-in customers on Dedicated + Hosted beta.
Canary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).
gates:
We will provide a set of preconfigured gates and allow custom metric expressions:
- Latency Gate: p95 increase <= 15% relative to baseline over gate window (default 15m).
- Error Gate: request 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute (sliding 15m).
- Decode Failure Gate: any spike > 3x baseline triggers immediate fail.
- Quality Gate: evaluated by running 200 golden prompts against new and baseline models and checking BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta; fail if quality drops > configured delta (default 2%).
- Resource Gate: GPU memory pressure > 80% sustained for 5m causes pause.
Gate evaluation semantics: each gate returns pass/warn/fail. A single fail triggers auto-rollback when automation is enabled. Warns pause ramp and require manual approval to continue.
instrumentation:
Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation time, 5xx counts, decode-fail counts, throughput, GPU memory/SM utilization.
Tracing: attach request-level traces to canary samples.
Logs: structured audit events for start/step/fail/rollback with controller run_id.
Synthetic checks: small harness that hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.
Dashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.
PRs and contracts: routing-api PR (github.com/redwood/re-routing/pulls/212), controller proto (github.com/redwood/re-release/pulls/37).
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Overly aggressive auto-rollback causing noisy rollbacks for transient spikes. Mitigation: use smoothing windows, require sustained failure for X samples or use majority of gates failing rather than single noisy metric.
Risk: Quality gate adds cost/time. Mitigation: sample fewer golden prompts for fast gates and run full quality suite during longer wait windows.
Risk: Stateful migrations, backward-incompatible cache formats. Mitigation: short-circuit routing to warm KV caches and run data-migration job in parallel; document supported migration patterns for LTS channels.
Risk: Console automation dependency creates blast radius. Mitigation: default automation OFF for new customers; require opt-in and RBAC for manual overrides.
